name: BERRY, Carol

headline.note: Two dated public-sector spells and six dated nonprofit spells are documented, but no source establishes substantive full-time status. Nonprofit, party, political-staff and elected-office spells are excluded from both headline sectors. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Family Planning Australia (historical legal/employer name not verified)
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech calls this one of her first jobs and describes reproductive-rights campaign work. Dates, hours and the employer's then-current legal name remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the codebook; no full-time duration inferred.

career_spells.evidence_note: A Greens publication identifies Berry as national secretary in 2004. Appointment endpoints, pay and hours are not established.
career_spells.counting_note: Party-organisation activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of Michael Organ MP (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: A Greens publication identifies Berry as an adviser to Cunningham MP Michael Organ in 2004. Exact appointment/payroll dates, leave and hours are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile index supplies month endpoints; first speech and biographies corroborate public-interest/human-rights legal work and disability-rights test cases. Hours and leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Professional-profile index supplies month endpoints and Executive Director title; a 2009 NSW Parliament submission independently records that role. Later biographies use CEO. Hours and leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile index supplies month endpoints; first speech and biographies corroborate the CEO role. Same-month transitions do not establish overlap or full-time hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Professional-profile index supplies month endpoints; official frozen occupation text and biographies corroborate title and disability-oversight work. Hours and leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is clear, but substantive full-time status is not; no headline duration counted.

career_spells.role: Director, Market Development; provider engagement and market development
career_spells.evidence_note: Professional-profile index supplies month endpoints; employer and role are corroborated by the later employer's welcome announcement and other biographies. Senior title does not establish hours; leave remains unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is clear, but substantive full-time status is not; no headline duration counted.

career_spells.evidence_note: Employer records say she joined in November 2020 as General Manager, Southern Operations, and moved to CEO in January 2023. Hours and leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Employer records give January 2023 CEO commencement and immediate cessation announced 5 May 2025 after the election. The announcement describes four and a half total years at the Trust. Hours and leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Frozen roster records service from 3 May 2025; ongoing at snapshot. The two-day calendar overlap with Trust cessation is preserved and not double-counted.

open_questions: What were the exact dates, legal employer and hours for the Family Planning role?
What were the appointment/payroll dates, pay status, hours and leave for the Greens national-secretary and Michael Organ adviser roles?
Were the dated PIAC, CID, IWHC, NSW Ombudsman, NDIA and Disability Trust spells substantively full-time, and were there material leave or breaks?
Do primary employer or government personnel records refine the month-only transitions and explain the 3–5 May 2025 Trust/House overlap?
